modules.module_title: Conduct regular inspection of machinery and equipment

pcs.pc_description: Conduct inspections according to a predetermined schedule (e.g., weekly, monthly, quarterly) to ensure comprehensive coverage of machinery and equipment.
Ensure that all scheduled inspections are completed within the specified timeframe to maintain consistency and reliability in identifying potential issues.
Verify that inspections are conducted meticulously, covering all critical components, parts, and subsystems of machinery and equipment.
Ensure adherence to established inspection protocols and checklists to minimize oversight.
Demonstrate the ability to accurately identify potential issues, anomalies, or deviations from normal operating conditions during inspections.
Document and report identified issues promptly to facilitate timely intervention and preventive measures.
Evaluate the accuracy of assessments made during inspections, including the severity and likelihood of identified issues.
Utilize appropriate diagnostic tools and techniques to enhance the precision of assessments.
Report inspection findings promptly to relevant stakeholders, including maintenance teams, supervisors, and management.
Ensure that reports are delivered within established timeframes to facilitate timely decision-making and action.
Maintain detailed and accurate records of inspection findings, including observations, measurements, and recommended actions.

modules.module_title: Assist in Design, Development and Implemention of predictive maintenance system

pcs.pc_description: Ensure that the acquired data is accurate and reliable to avoid misleading analysis.
Measure accuracy through comparison with known standards or manual inspections where applicable.
Acquire all necessary data required for predictive maintenance analysis.
Verify that all relevant parameters and variables are included in the dataset.
Ensure consistency in data format, units, and timestamps across all acquired datasets.
Resolve any discrepancies or inconsistencies found during the acquisition process.
Acquire data in a timely manner to ensure that it reflects the current state of the equipment or system.
Minimize delays between data acquisition and analysis to enable timely decision-making.
Acquire data that is directly relevant to the predictive maintenance objectives.
Filter out irrelevant data to streamline analysis and improve efficiency.
Implement measures to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of acquired data.
Adhere to relevant data privacy regulations and organizational policies.
Perform data quality checks and validation procedures to identify and correct errors or anomalies.
Implement automated quality control measures where possible to ensure consistent data quality.
PC15. Optimize data acquisition processes to minimize resource utilization and maximize efficiency
Optimize data acquisition processes to minimize resource utilization and maximize efficiency.
Utilize automated data acquisition systems where appropriate to reduce manual effort and human error.
Implement data management practices to organize, catalog, and archive acquired datasets effectively
Maintain comprehensive documentation of data acquisition processes, including metadata such as sensor configurations and sampling rates.
Ensure that acquired data is well- documented and annotated to facilitate analysis and interpretation.
Design data acquisition systems and processes to accommodate future scalability and evolving maintenance requirements.
Ensure flexibility to adapt to changes in equipment configurations or monitoring objectives.
Ensure compatibility and interoperability between data acquisition systems and analysis tools.
Facilitate seamless integration of acquired data with existing predictive maintenance workflows and platforms.

pcs.pc_description: take measurements (using appropriate tools/techniques/technologies) of various parameters for condition monitoring for each equipment in the predetermined route
establish, in specific cases, the quality of the measurements by elimination of the common causes of poor measurements (e.g. poor mounting of the transducer, transducer fault)
take measurements/note down values of other relevant parameters of the equipment (e.g. process data/operation data like pressure, temperature, flow)
record the conditions in which the measurements were taken (e.g. operating speed, equipment load, ambient temperature)
observe and note down any specific physical conditions of the equipment (e.g. leakage, low level, looseness, wear and tear)
download the measured data into the related data storage and analysis software system, as applicable for further analysis

modules.module_title: Process the data and perform analysis by trending

pcs.pc_description: acquire the raw‑data, filter out unwanted noise and/or other non‑related signals, and format the measured signals in the form required for further analysis and diagnosis
compare the measured values to historical trends (e.g. overall values like vibration velocity in rms, temperature, current)
compare the measured values to baseline data (e.g. baseline readings taken during commissioning of the equipment)
compare the measured values to representative data for the same or similar equipment

evaluate data as per criteria for the severity of the parameter (e.g. vibration severity based on the vibration magnitude at rated speed under steady operation conditions and significant changes, in either direction, in the magnitude of the vibration, including the rate of change); look for any other anomaly in the data

modules.module_title: Compare measurement to alerts/alarm criteria for the equipment

pcs.pc_description: check whether the measured values are acceptable compared to the alert/alarm criteria for the equipment (e.g. measured bearing temperature and the alarm limit) and determine if operation of the equipment may continue for a period till the time investigations are carried out to identify the reason for the change in the measured parameter and define any remedial action

determine the need for any immediate action on the equipment (e.g. reduction of load, greasing of the bearing), as necessary, other than to record the value and observations and to continue to monitor the equipment
decide on the need for any additional measurements and monitoring (e.g. at more/different locations)
determine the need for any short-term change in frequency of the condition monitoring (e.g. once every two weeks to week or weekly to daily) till the time the equipment behaviour is normal

• initiate the diagnosis process in case the measured values are not acceptable compared to the alert/alarm criteria for the equipment • note: consider the need for diagnosis even on other occasions when no anomalies are suspected or detected (e.g. condition assessment of an equipment before a major shutdown to determine the need for any maintenance action or when other symptoms like noise, smell are detected outside of condition monitoring, e.g. operator surveillance)
consider the basic approaches (e.g. the time domain and the frequency domain analysis) when analyzing certain signals like vibration, current (e.g. time waveform and spectrum)

data measured on the equipment at various locations and directions (e.g. condition data, related process/operation data and other data like load, startup/shutdown); other physical conditions/observations on the equipment
in case of any issues in the quality of the measurements, cause/s for the same and corrective action (e.g. replace/calibrate the transducer or the cable)
findings based on preliminary evaluation of data (trends, magnitude, rate of change, correlation with any other parameter)
decisions based on the analysis (e.g. additional data collection, changes to condition monitoring frequency, time domain and frequency domain analysis)
recommendations based on the analysis (equipment load/speed reduction, lubrication, shutdown in case of exceeding the trip value/s)
need for diagnosis for identification of the issue/s

modules.module_title: Establish diagnostic requirements for the condition monitoring setup

pcs.pc_description: understand the essential role of diagnostics in decision making for appropriate operation or maintenance tasks based on condition data analysis
be able to set up diagnostic procedures according to the faults that can occur in the equipment
carry out preliminary study when preparing the requirements for condition monitoring and diagnostics of equipment (for appropriate condition data necessary for diagnosis, diagnostic techniques)

understand the various steps generally applied to the diagnostic study and the application of Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA)/ Failure Mode and Effect Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and Failure Mode Symptoms Analysis (FMSA)

prepare diagnostics requirements report, clearly identifying the equipment faults that are not covered by condition monitoring and hence are not diagnosable (e.g. information about the equipment; failure modes/symptoms analysis)

re-evaluate, on an ongoing basis, the value of adding more capability (e.g. diagnostic tools and techniques, related condition data measurements) to detect specific equipment faults not covered initially

• understand the condition monitoring data in terms of • a) measurements, • b) descriptors, • c) symptoms, • d) fault, • e) operational parameters (used for establishing descriptors or establishing operating conditions)

• understand machine data, e.g. • a) for vibrations – speed, number of gear teeth, rolling element bearing fault frequencies • b) for oil analysis – oil flow, metal composition, filter ratings • c) for current analysis – no. of stator bars, no. of rotor slots
understand the machine history in terms of fault history, operational history and maintenance history
understand the triggers for the diagnosis (e.g. detection of an anomaly during routine monitoring of the equipment)

detect anomaly (e.g. by appropriate methods like making a comparison between the present descriptors of the equipment or comparison with similar equipment) in the equipment that warrants the need for diagnosis
identify the change in one or more of the measured or derived parameters from the baseline values that are indicative of potential fault
understand the various considerations for selection of appropriate diagnostic approach/es (e.g. application of the equipment, monitoring technique, data availability)

• determine the best possible approach (in the legacy environment) for diagnosing the condition of an equipment • 1. data-driven approach (e.g. simple trending, histograms) • 2. knowledge-based approach (e.g. fault models) • note: In many cases the use of both the approaches may be necessary

• decide on the knowledge-based approach to be used for legacy environment • 1. the faults/symptoms approach and • 2. the causal approach (for in-depth knowledge of the mechanism of the initiation and fault propagation)

estimate the confidence in the accuracy of the diagnosis based on the consideration for various elements (e.g. maintenance history with experience of same fault on similar machines, analysis technique)
decide on further verification as required based on the confidence in the diagnosis
carryout the necessary actions to increase the confidence in the diagnosis (e.g. retaking measurements, additional measurements, more sophisticated diagnostic process or measurement technique)

modules.module_title: Decide on the prognosis and prognostic approaches

pcs.pc_description: based on the diagnosis and the expected progression of existing and future faults, estimate the need for prognosis

decide on the need for fault prognosis based on the diagnosis based on foreknowledge of the probable failure modes, future duties to which the machine will or might be subjected, and a thorough understanding of the relationships between failure modes and operating conditions
understand the requirement of various data for prognosis
understand the basics of a prognosis process (preprocessing to post-action prognosis)
understand the influence factors (parameters that affect the deterioration rate of a failure mode and hence impacts the time to failure)
determine the need to establish the estimated time to failure (ETTF)
understand the requirements of a prognosis report
perform fault prognosis to estimate the time to failure
carryout the necessary actions to increase the confidence in the prognosis (e.g. retaking measurements, additional measurements, more sophisticated diagnostic process or measurement technique)
prepare diagnostics requirements report
prepare diagnosis report
take actions to increase the confidence in the diagnosis
prepare prognosis report
take actions to increase the confidence in the prognosis

modules.module_title: Determine the need for maintenance action

pcs.pc_description: determine the action/s to be taken on the equipment (e.g. no action, increase or decrease the equipment load/speed/throughput)
determine the need for an immediate shutdown of the equipment based on severity of the fault conditions (e.g. based on alert/alarm limits for the measured parameter)
determine the need for maintenance action (e.g. inspection of the equipment or corrective maintenance work) based on the level of confidence in the fault diagnosis and prognosis
recommend the maintenance action to the equipment owner operator and/or maintenance team (e.g. email or verbal communication or portal)
create a Maintenance Work Request/Notification in the CMMS/EAM System if the organization’s business processes support such an action

modules.module_title: Record maintenance activities performed and the equipment condition post maintenance

pcs.pc_description: record the details of maintenance action performed on the equipment including inspection findings, spares used, other faults discovered during inspection/restoration of the equipment

record the changes to the equipment condition, post maintenance action (e.g. reduction in vibration post alignment of the driven and driver equipment, reduction in temperature post greasing of the bearing)
validate the recommendations given post analysis, diagnosis and prognosis for their effectiveness by inspection of the component/s (e.g. bearing condition, misalignment)

capture all the maintenance work and the equipment condition in the equipment history record for reference in future diagnosis and prognosis, review of effectiveness of the predictive maintenance program

where appropriate (e.g. repetitive failures of an equipment), support review and optimization of the maintenance strategy for the equipment (e.g. introduction of new condition monitoring technique, additional maintenance tasks for PM, design-out maintenance as necessary)
prepare documentation on recommendations for the action to be taken
prepare documentation on recommendation for maintenance of the equipment
prepare documentation on work request/maintenance notification initiated for maintenance interventions
prepare documentation on maintenance work carried out including physical observations, findings
prepare documentation on changes to the equipment condition, post maintenance action
prepare documentation on changes to the equipment maintenance strategy

modules.module_title: Periodical review of the condition monitoring/predictive maintenance program

pcs.pc_description: review the condition monitoring/predictive maintenance program on a periodical basis, for various aspects (e.g. feasibility of adopting condition monitoring techniques not implemented earlier, effectiveness of condition monitoring and diagnostic techniques currently implemented)
revise alert/alarm criteria due to changes in the equipment being monitored considering the various aspects (e.g. progressive wear of the components, ageing, operation/duty cycle changes)
re-establish baselines where required (e.g. post-equipment overhaul/modification/rerating)
modify rule-based diagnostics where applicable (e.g. changes to the components, limits of the parameters)
issue of condition monitoring and diagnostic reports within the timeline/agreed time window
regularly back up all data in a secure manner
review, update and revise data bases (e.g. different, disparate condition monitoring systems/solutions) at pre-determined intervals
review alarm settings at regular intervals
prepare documentation on report of the periodical review of the predictive maintenance program including the recommendations

prepare documentation on secure back up of all data carried out on periodical basis
prepare documentation on review/update/revisions carried out for various data bases and software
review and revisions carried out to alarm settings at regular intervals

modules.module_title: Adhere to standard safety procedures of the organisation

pcs.pc_description: comply with general safety procedures and those for handling equipment, tools, chemicals, and hazardous material, as prescribed and followed in the organisation
remove finger rings or any other metal objects likely to interfere with the work
ensure that identification badge or any other object worn around the neck or on the clothing does not get caught in any rotating machine, or otherwise interfere with the work
use appropriate safety devices such as goggles, gloves, ear plugs, caps, ESD pins, covers, shoes, helmets etc. recommended for the work being performed
inform, escalate, or raise alarm about any suspicions, unaccounted hazardous material, devices, or other objects found in the premises

avoid damage to sensitive electronic components due to negligence of ESD procedures
participate regularly in fire drills or other safety related workshops organised by the organisation

proceed to designated safe assembly area immediately on hearing fire alarm

follow common personal hygiene practices

participate in company organised health sessions such as exercises, games, yoga, physiotherapy, and other activities
